How Hard Would It Be For Eloro Resources To Raise More Cash For Growth?

data.title: Don't Ignore The Insider Selling In Newell Brands
data.description:
Anyone interested in Newell Brands Inc. (NASDAQ:NWL) should probably be aware that the President, Christopher Peterson, recently divested US$295k worth of shares in the company, at an average price of US$5.90 each. On the bright side, that sale was only 1.7% of their holding, so we doubt it's very meaningful, on its own.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Newell Brands

Over the last year, we can see that the biggest insider sale was by the Chief Legal & Administrative Officer and Corporate Secretary, Bradford Turner, for US$616k worth of shares, at about US$6.16 per share. That means that an insider was selling shares at around the current price of US$5.67. We generally don't like to see insider selling, but the lower the sale price, the more it concerns us. We note that this sale took place at around the current price, so it isn't a major concern, though it's hardly a good sign.

Insiders in Newell Brands didn't buy any shares in the last year. You can see the insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last year depicted in the chart below. If you want to know exactly who sold, for how much, and when, simply click on the graph below!

Insider Ownership Of Newell Brands

Looking at the total insider shareholdings in a company can help to inform your view of whether they are well aligned with common shareholders. A high insider ownership often makes company leadership more mindful of shareholder interests. Newell Brands insiders own about US$35m worth of shares. That equates to 1.5% of the company. This level of insider ownership is good but just short of being particularly stand-out. It certainly does suggest a reasonable degree of alignment.

So What Does This Data Suggest About Newell Brands Insiders?

An insider sold stock recently, but they haven't been buying. Looking to the last twelve months, our data doesn't show any insider buying. Insiders own shares, but we're still pretty cautious, given the history of sales. We'd practice some caution before buying!
